I want you to solve GitHub issue #3130: implement the fix, validate it,
commit it, and report. Read this entire brief, then the repository AGENTS.md
and its relevant routed guidance. Do not stop at a survey or plan. If the issue
and repository genuinely leave a decision open, ask the judge one specific
question and wait for the answer, then continue.

# Working agreement

Your repository is the `bifrost` checkout under /workspace in your own container
(mj 2.10.0 places it at /workspace/<workspace id>/bifrost; `ls /workspace/*/bifrost`
finds it). The judge is Claude Fable.
All competing lanes receive this identical brief. Do not inspect other lanes,
their sessions, the judge's private files, or evaluation results about this issue.
Before investigation, verify your checkout has no tracked or untracked changes,
fetch origin, and check out this exact commit detached: 844ca7606768b8dd504d3cd23af038a612e1f35a
The detached checkout is explicitly authorized for this evaluation. Report its
full hash. Do not merge newer master or change the base during your initial run.

Work only in your container. Commit your changes on the detached HEAD, with
real messages. Do not push, create branches or PRs, edit issue labels, or post
GitHub comments. The judge exports your commits. Commit all intended work before
your final report; never stage unrelated files or use git add -A.
Do not write to any memory directory or MEMORY.md: that pool is shared across
sessions and harnesses. Keep discoveries in your report. Do not read other
evaluation sessions or their reports. Do not launch subagents; do the entire
solution in this lane, so every configuration has the same delegation policy.

Use plain cargo and the repository testing guidance. Clear JAVA_HOME and set
BIFROST_PARALLELISM=1 and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1. Let nextest own concurrency;
pass --max-fail 100. Run relevant crate and integration suites. Changes under a
language's graph code or analysis usages require that language's usage and issue
suites plus cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost-analysis --lib.
Run cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings and
format changed files. Do not reduce nextest concurrency without measured resource
exhaustion. Report pre-existing failures only after checking the same base.
The harness fails a turn after 10 minutes without activity, so never block on
one command for longer than 5 minutes: run long builds and suites in the
background or with a timeout of at most 300000 ms and poll their output.
Never run shared-cache GC or delete another session's build targets. If disk
pressure requires isolated storage, use the repository's managed target helper.

Fix causes with tree-sitter and analyzer structures, not source-text parsing or
regex fallbacks. Use assertions for construction invariants, iterative traversal
for deep trees, plain ASCII, and the existing shared helpers. Demonstrate a
production-shaped regression failing before and passing after the fix.
Read relevant architecture chapters before changing identities, cache, usage,
dataflow, semantic models or results. Bump the language extraction epoch when
the persisted language facts change; do not bump it for query-only changes.
Use an ExecPlan under .agents/plans only when the repository requires one.

External evidence repositories are not preinstalled: fetch the issue's pinned
commits under /workspace/evidence, outside this checkout. Use a fresh analyzer
cache at /workspace/cache when needed. Validate the actual witnesses and census
coverage, not merely a lower finding count caused by sampling or suppression.

# Reporting

An ordinary end of turn is not completion. When finished, commit your solution
and send a message with FINAL REPORT on its own line within the first five lines,
followed by these six sections:
1. Confirmed cause with structured evidence.
2. Changes and reasons, including full base and final commit hashes.
3. Exact validation commands and results.
4. Before/after evidence on the issue's named repositories or witnesses.

Comment by DavidBakerEffendi:
Implementation checkpoint for the CSMI-backed prerequisite:

- CSMI PR #35 is merged and publishes the exact `csmi.collection-flow` 0.1.0 contract.
- Bifrost now imports, validates, persists, activates, and looks up typed collection-flow contracts.
- The Scala standard-library pack emits exact `scala.collection.mutable.Map[K,V]` contracts for `apply`, `update`, and tuple-entry `foreach`, including receiver generic substitution and explicit key/value entry components.
- Scala lowering consumes those active contracts for indexed map storage/loading and tuple-pattern projection. A custom `Map` near miss remains unmodeled.
- The semantic-model snapshot is frozen into threaded Scala lowering so call-site consumption uses the same active-model generation as artifact derivation.

Validation on the rebased branch:

- `cargo fmt --check`: pass
- `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD`: pass
- `node scripts/check-open-core-classification.mjs`: pass
- `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 cargo check -p brokk-bifrost-analysis --tests --message-format short`: pass
- `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 cargo clippy -p brokk-bifrost-analysis --lib --tests -- -D warnings`: pass
- producer/activation focused nextest slice: 3/3 pass
- end-to-end Scala semantic slice: 3/3 pass after rebase; a later repeat exhausted local disk while linking unrelated root binaries, before test execution

This is deliberately a prerequisite rather than closure for #3130. CSMI collection flow does not prove callback execution/count/termination or the remaining control-flow protocol, so the full DataFlowBench scenario remains inconclusive and this issue should stay open.

FINAL REPORT

## 1. Confirmed cause with structured evidence

Base commit `844ca7606768b8dd504d3cd23af038a612e1f35a` already contains #3166 (`435327366d15f1b5822d6462743cc0633ff55281`) as an ancestor, so of the two gaps named in the issue only one was still open:

- The `array_index_access`/update gap is **closed by #3166**, not by this commit. Its `csmi.collection-flow` 0.1.0 contract retains exact `scala.collection.mutable.Map[K, V]` identity and lowers `records("record") = value` to a keyed `MemoryStore { kind: Index }`. Re-measuring the base with the real Scala-library pack producer and activation (committed fixtures, base `semantic.rs`) shows the store lowering and a partially resolved finding, not a missing update model: `map-iteration-positive expected=reached observed=reached complete=false findings=3`, and the same for `guard` and `yield`.
- The still-open gap is exactly `for_expression`. Before this change the adapter admitted no comprehension to a modeled path: it scheduled only the *first* enumerator's source expression plus the body, and emitted the blanket protocol gaps. Since `emit_local_bindings`/`tuple_pattern_bindings` returned bare identifiers (and dropped `_` by position), a `(key, value) <- records` enumerator read no aggregate entry and bound no value. Base outputs: `map-iteration-negative observed=inconclusive complete=false findings=0`, `map-iteration-nested observed=inconclusive complete=false findings=0`, `map-iteration-wildcard-key observed=inconclusive complete=false` (from `/tmp/runs/final_before_measure.log`; negative/nested from the pre-fix run `/tmp/runs/baseline2.log`, since the pinned assertions abort a test at its first mismatching row).
- The frozen DataFlowBench v0.7.1 report (`/workspace/evidence/DataFlowBench/reports/bifrost-scala-kernel.json`) records both cases as `inconclusive` with `procedure value-flow snapshot for MapIteration{Positive,Negative}.scala:....run is unsupported (assignments)`.

## 2. Changes and reasons

Base `844ca7606768b8dd504d3cd23af038a612e1f35a` → final `9b955abe8ae86c030eb71be18235f05e096bc3c7` (single commit, detached HEAD, not pushed).

- `crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/scala/semantic.rs` (`ADAPTER_VERSION` v14 → v15; lowering facts change, no extraction-epoch change):
  - New `Work::ForEnumeratorStage` + `ForStage::{Generator, Guard}`. `for_expression` first tries `modeled_for_stages`; the admission is all-or-nothing, so an unproven receiver or unsupported shape keeps the original four blanket protocol gaps unchanged.
  - `modeled_for_stages` reads only tree-sitter fields (`enumerators`, `generator`, `guard`, `pattern`, `rhs`) plus the activated contract. A generator needs a `tuple_pattern` and an rhs the `foreach` contract proves as the keyed collection; a guard is either the inline `guard` child of a generator enumerator or a guard-only brace enumerator. The value binder is chosen by the contract's named value component, not by written order or name.
  - `modeled_for_expression` lowers one conditional per stage in source order, body loops back with `LoopBack`, false arms leave the comprehension, and `yield` adds a point-scoped `Values`/`Unsupported` gap because the result collection is not constructed.
  - `for_enumerator_stage` evaluates the source, adds `MemoryLocationKind::Index { identity: Aggregate }` + `MemoryLoad{Index}`, flows the entry into the value binder, publishes one non-blocking point-scoped `Calls`/`Unsupported` gap for the desugared `map`/`flatMap`/`withFilter`/`foreach` call it deliberately does not fabricate, and adds both conditional edges.
  - `tuple_pattern_bindings` now returns `(slot, identifier)` pairs from top-level named children, preserving wildcard slots and nested-pattern slots; `emit_local_bindings` records each binder with its `component_index`. `modeled_keyed_collection` is the single shared proof used by both construction and iteration.
  - I did not re-implement the Map construction/access/update model: #3166 already covers it, as me

was still open (positive reached but incomplete; negative and nested generators inconclusive). I added a per-enumerator lowering that admits a comprehension only when every enumerator is either a generator whose right-hand side an active `csmi.collection-flow` contract proves as the keyed collection, or a guard. Each stage becomes one conditional in source order, the body loops back, and a generator reads one aggregate entry and projects the contract's named value component into the tuple binder at that component slot, so `(key, _)` stays clean while `(_, value)` carries taint. Everything reads tree-sitter fields (`enumerators`, `generator`, `guard`, `pattern`, `rhs`) and the activated contract; there is no name check, source-text parsing, or benchmark-shaped flow, and an unproven receiver keeps the old four-gap path so it can never inherit standard-library iteration or fake a clean negative. The desugared `map`/`flatMap`/`withFilter`/`foreach` call is deliberately not fabricated as a call site; each generator records that omission as a point-scoped, non-blocking `Calls` gap, and `yield` keeps a `Values` gap because the result collection is not constructed. The pair now decides (positive reached with `complete=true`, negative clean with `complete=true`), and the same lowering holds for the guard, guard-only enumerator, nested-generator, and yield fixtures; the custom same-terminal receiver stays inconclusive. Validation: full `suite_semantic` 1793/1793, Scala slices of usages/issues/symbols 280/137/52, `brokk-bifrost-analysis --lib` 3050/3050, formatting, scoped clippy, and open-core classification pass; workspace clippy fails only on a pre-existing `clone_on_copy` outside this change. One caveat worth a follow-up: the DataFlowBench adapter supplies no dependency evidence and the CLI then rejects the installed Scala-library pack with a shard-selector mismatch, reproducible without any comprehension, so the DFB harness could not be replayed end to end in-container and the acceptance harness above was used instead.
